forward_guidance.text: Q3 2026: strong sales and revenues growth versus Q3 2025 in all three primary segments, driven by higher volume and favorable price realization (Resource Industries price benefit smaller than in Q2). Tariff costs of about $600M expected in Q3. Profit impact of volume and price is expected to be partly offset by unfavorable manufacturing costs and higher SG&A/R&D. Construction Industries dealer inventory is expected to rise slightly in Q3, modestly less than Q3 2025. Full-year 2026: sales and revenues growth now expected in the mid-to-high teens; tariff costs of about $2.2B excluding IEEPA recoveries, with no additional IEEPA recoveries assumed in H2; restructuring costs of $300-350M; capex of about $3.5B; annual effective tax rate of 23.0% excluding discrete items. Construction Industries dealer inventory is expected to fall by over $1.0B in Q4 but end 2026 higher than year-end 2025, an unfavorable H2 volume effect. Capacity expansion is expected to raise throughput in H2 2026. No explicit EPS or margin guidance is given in the 10-Q.
forward_guidance.source_citation: 10-Q Item 2 MD&A, Trends and Economic Conditions: Third-Quarter 2026 and Full-Year 2026 Company Trends and Expectations; Restructuring Costs

key_risks.description: Tariff exposure: about $600M of tariff costs expected in Q3 and about $2.2B for FY2026 (excluding recoveries). Resource Industries H1 profit decline is largely attributed to higher tariff costs.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Item 2 MD&A, Trends and Economic Conditions; Resource Industries (six months); Forward-looking Statements (v)

key_risks.description: Uncertainty over IEEPA tariff refunds: $392M was recorded as probable in Q2, but the rest of the approx. $1.0B of IEEPA costs is not deemed probable. Long-term receivables include $1.2B of import overpayment recoveries, and CBP review timing is uncertain. The refund benefit flattered Q2 profit.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part I Note 1, Basis of presentation; Item 2 MD&A Global Business Conditions

key_risks.description: Dealer inventory and Construction Industries volume: dealer inventory built 2.6B in H1 (CI +1.9B). Management expects a Q4 destock of over 1.0B and an unfavorable H2 inventory effect on CI volume, so Q2/H1 results may overstate end-user demand.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Item 2 MD&A, Consolidated Sales and Revenues (six months); Full-Year 2026 Company Trends and Expectations

key_risks.description: Cost pressure: unfavorable manufacturing costs (higher period costs) and higher SG&A/R&D are expected to offset part of volume and price gains. This compressed Power & Energy and Resource Industries profit in the period.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Item 2 MD&A, Power & Energy and Resource Industries; Third-Quarter 2026 Company Trends

key_risks.description: Cat Financial credit quality: write-offs rose to 46M gross in Q2 from 27M, and the provision rose to 29M from 21M. Non-accrual customer receivables were 178M vs 163M at year-end 2025, with Latin America and EAME non-accruals rising.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part I Note 17, Cat Financial financing activities

key_risks.description: Capital allocation and leverage: cash fell to 6.7B from 10.0B on buybacks of 6.5B and the RPMGlobal acquisition. Financial Products debt rose 1.8B. Shareholders' equity fell to 19.4B on repurchases and ASR forward contracts. The 3.5B 364-day credit facility expires in August 2026. Covenant headroom remains ample (net worth 19.5B vs 9.0B minimum).
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Item 1 Consolidated Statement of Financial Position; Item 2 MD&A Liquidity and Capital Resources

bull_case: Q2 revenue grew 24% with operating margin up 360bp to 20.9% (21.9% adjusted); adjusted EPS of $8.17 was up about 73% year over year.
Backlog rose to about $72.1B (+$9.4B sequentially) with orders up across all three primary segments, giving multi-quarter visibility.
Power Generation sales grew 29% on data center demand, with turbines and large reciprocating engines in demand and capacity expansion expected to lift H2 throughput.
Management raised FY2026 growth guidance to mid-to-high teens and expects strong Q3 growth in all primary segments, helped by favorable price realization.
Cash generation is strong: H1 MP&E free cash flow was $5.7B (vs $2.6B), supporting dividend growth (+8% to $1.63) and $8.4B of remaining buyback authorization.

Construction Industries end-user demand is strong (North America end-user sales up), and Resource Industries has robust orders with copper and gold demand. The RPMGlobal acquisition adds mining software.
Cat Financial credit metrics are stable to improving (past dues 1.31% vs 1.62%), and Financial Products segment profit rose 32%.
bear_case: Q2 profit included a $392M IEEPA tariff recovery that likely will not repeat. Excluding it, margin gains would be smaller, and H2 guidance assumes no further recoveries.
Tariff costs remain heavy (about $600M in Q3 and about $2.2B for FY2026), and manufacturing cost and SG&A/R&D increases are expected to offset part of volume and price gains.
Resource Industries H1 profit fell 10% with margin down to 12.7% from 15.7%, and Q2 margin was only 14.9%.
H1 growth was inflated by dealer restocking (dealer inventory +2.6B vs +0.2B). Q4 destocking of over $1.0B in Construction Industries will be a headwind, so the Q3 comparison must be watched.
Q3 price realization in Resource Industries is guided lower than in Q2, and sales growth comparisons get harder after a strong first half.

Balance sheet and cash are being drawn down: cash fell $3.3B in six months, Financial Products debt rose, working capital rose (inventories +$2.5B, receivables +$3.2B), and the equity base is shrinking from buybacks.
Cat Financial write-offs and provisions rose year over year, non-accruals increased in Latin America and EAME, and Asia Pacific outside China and the Middle East are soft.

what_to_watch.text: Q3 2026 results versus guidance: strong sales growth in all three primary segments, about $600M of tariff costs, and whether margins hold without the Q2 IEEPA recovery benefit.

Further IEEPA refund claims: any additional recoveries accepted through CBP's CAPE system, timing of collection of the $1.2B long-term and $130M current receivables, and whether the FY tariff estimate of about $2.2B changes.
Backlog level and mix (was $72.1B), especially Power & Energy turbine and reciprocating engine orders tied to data centers, and the share of backlog beyond 12 months ($29.2B).
Construction Industries dealer inventory trends: Q3 build slightly lower than Q3 2025, the Q4 destock of over $1.0B, and sell-through to end users.
Resource Industries margin recovery, RPMGlobal contribution and manufacturing cost headwinds, and the pace of H2 capacity throughput increases.

Capital return and liquidity: final settlement of the ASR agreements (Q4 2026), buyback pace against $8.4B remaining, the 364-day credit facility renewal (expires August 2026), and Cat Financial credit metrics.
